studies.Title: Total antioxidant intake and prostate cancer in the Cancer of the Prostate in Sweden (CAPS) study. A case control study.
studies.Reference: Total antioxidant intake and prostate cancer in the Cancer of the Prostate in Sweden (CAPS) study. A case control study.
studies.Timing: Diet was assessed after diagnosis; the questionnaire was sent an average of 5 months after diagnosis.
studies.Population: Men in the population-based Cancer of the Prostate in Sweden study, including incident prostate cancer cases and population controls.
studies.comparison_type: Above-median supplemental TAC intake among users compared with non-users

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: For antioxidant intake from supplements we found a positive association with total, advanced, localized, high grade and low grade prostate cancer in those above median supplemental TAC intake of users compared to non-users (Adjusted ORs for total prostate cancer: 1.37, 95 % CI 1.08-1.73, advanced: 1.51, 95 % CI 1.11-2.06, localized: 1.36. 95 % CI 1.06-1.76, high grade 1.60, 95 % CI 1.06-2.40, low grade 1.36, 95 % CI 1.03-1.81).
extraction_supporting_text.cases: We used FFQ data from 1499 cases and 1112 controls in the population based case-control study Cancer of the Prostate in Sweden (CAPS).
